Agent Skills for use with Obsidian.

These skills follow the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification), so they work with any agent that supports skills, including Claude Code, Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Kiro, Muse, OpenCode, and [many more](https://agentskills.io/clients).

## Installation

Obsidian is an official plugin for Claude, ChatGPT, Dots, Cursor, Grok Bot, Hermes, and Kiro. Most other agents can install the skills from GitHub.

### Claude

Add [Obsidian](https://claude.ai/customize/plugins/id/a38fa062-ebd3-48e0-9a0a-1875a6e94ad5%40anthropic-plugin-directory) from the official Claude plugin directory.

For the Claude Code CLI use:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
claude plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

From within a Claude Code session:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
/plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

To get new skills later, run `claude plugin update obsidian@obsidian-skills`.

### ChatGPT

Add [Obsidian](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aee4fde227881919d61b034b1c31096) from the ChatGPT plugin directory. The plugin works in ChatGPT, Codex, and Dots.

To install from this repo instead:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

Then install Obsidian from the plugin directory in Codex or the ChatGPT desktop app.

### Antigravity

In the Antigravity CLI, run:

```sh
agy plugin install https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

### Grok Bot

Open [Obsidian for Grok Bot](https://x.ai/bot/plugin/88871845) and select **Add to Grok Bot**.

### Muse

Ask Muse to install the skills from https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills.

Muse runs in Meta's cloud, so the `obsidian-cli` skill doesn't work there. If you use Obsidian Headless in Muse, you sign in and sync your vault in Meta's cloud.

### Cursor

Install [Obsidian](https://cursor.com/marketplace/obsidian) from the Cursor Marketplace.

### Hermes Agent

Install [Obsidian](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/marketplace/obsidian) from the Hermes Marketplace, or run:

```sh
hermes plugins install obsidian
```

```sh
kiro-cli powers install obsidian
```

Install with [npx skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), which asks which agents to install into:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
```

candidates.description: Teleprompter para Linux: tu guion bajo la cámara, avanza mientras hablas
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Mirada

**Teleprompter para Linux.** Muestra tu guion en una franja pegada al borde superior de la pantalla, justo bajo la cámara, para que leas mientras mantienes contacto visual. El texto avanza mientras hablas y se detiene cuando haces una pausa.

[English](README.en.md) · Licencia [MIT](LICENSE)

![Mirada bajo la webcam](docs/img/hero.png)

![Demo: el texto avanza mientras hablas y se detiene en las pausas](docs/img/demo.gif)

## Características

- **Modo notch:** franja centrada bajo la webcam, siempre encima de las demás ventanas.
- **Modo flotante:** ventana que puedes mover y redimensionar.
- **Seguimiento por voz:** avanza solo mientras hablas (detecta volumen; no envía audio a ningún lado).
- **Secciones:** las líneas que empiezan con `#` se convierten en secciones a las que puedes saltar.
- **Control remoto** desde el teléfono en la misma Wi-Fi (opcional, desactivado por defecto).
- Modo espejo, cuenta regresiva, color y tamaño de letra, opacidad.

## Instalar

### Opción 1: paquete .deb o AppImage (recomendado)

Descarga el archivo de la [última versión](https://github.com/jleiva831/mirada/releases/latest) (cuando haya una publicada). Ambos traen su propio Python y Qt; no necesitan `pip`. Probados en Debian 12 y 13 y Ubuntu 22.04 y 24.04 (el AppImage, en cualquier distribución con glibc reciente). `apt` descarga solo las bibliotecas del sistema que falten (p. ej. `libxcb-cursor0`), así que necesita acceso a los repositorios de tu distribución.

```bash
# Debian 12+ / Ubuntu 22.04+ / Mint / Pop!_OS
sudo apt install ./mirada_VERSION_amd64.deb

# cualquier distribución x86_64
chmod +x Mirada-VERSION-x86_64.AppImage
./Mirada-VERSION-x86_64.AppImage
```

El `.deb` instala en `/opt/mirada` y crea el comando `mirada`; se desinstala con `sudo apt remove mirada`. El AppImage ya incluye `xcb-cursor` y PortAudio; para el seguimiento por voz el sistema necesita además ALSA (`libasound2`, y `libjack-jackd2-0` en sistemas mínimos), que cualquier escritorio normal ya trae; si tu sistema no tiene FUSE, ejecútalo con `--appimage-extract-and-run`. Para construirlos tú mismo: `bash packaging/build-deb.sh` y `bash packaging/build-appimage.sh` (resultado en `dist/`; ver `packaging/`).

### Opción 2: instalador

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jleiva831/mirada.git
cd mirada
bash install.sh
```

Instala todo en tu usuario (`~/.local`), sin sudo, y agrega Mirada al menú de aplicaciones.

pipx install git+https://github.com/jleiv

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Frontend Design skill for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor

A free agent skill that designs your UI before your agent builds it. It sends a short brief from your codebase to UX Pilot, which designs real screens on a canvas you can open and edit. Your agent then builds the screens you pick in your own stack, with your components and tokens. It works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any agent that supports skills and MCP.

## Install

```bash
npx skills add uxpilot-ai/frontend-design-skill
```

Or copy the `skills/ui-design` folder into your agent's skills folder (for Claude Code, `~/.claude/skills/`).

Then connect UX Pilot once. In Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http uxpilot https://mcp.uxpilot.net/mcp
```

Run `/mcp` in Claude Code and sign in. In Cursor and other agents, add the MCP server `https://mcp.uxpilot.net/mcp` and sign in. If you skip this, the skill walks you through it. A free UX Pilot account is enough to start.

## What it does

- Reads your project first: product, audience, routes, colors, fonts and copy, so the brief uses your real content.
- Designs the screens with UX Pilot and gives you a link to the canvas, where you can compare, edit and comment on them.
- Shows each screen in the chat and fixes common problems such as low contrast or clipped text.
- Builds the chosen screens in your code with your existing components, then checks the result against the design.
- Asks before every design run, because runs use UX Pilot credits.

## Example prompts

- "Design a better landing page for this app, then build it."
- "Redesign our pricing page. Keep our brand colors."
- "Design the onboarding screens for this mobile app."
- "Make this dashboard look less generic."

## What's inside

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | Connecting UX Pilot, writing the brief, running and showing the design |
| `references/implementing.md` | Building the design in your stack and checking it |

## Made by UX Pilot

[UX Pilot](https://uxpilot.ai/?utm_source=frontend-design-skill&utm_medium=readme) is an AI UI design tool for screens, user flows, prototypes and UX reviews.

## License

[Apache License 2.0](LICENSE): use, change and share it freely. Keep the [NOTICE](NOTICE) file when you do.

candidates.description: MCP server connecting AI assistants to the Spanish National Statistics Institute (INE) public API. Enables access to official demographic, economic and social statistics, making it easy to search, retrieve and analyze reliable data using natural language.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# INE MCP **Official statistics of Spain, straight from the source, for any AI assistant.** A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the public JSON API of **INE** (Instituto Nacional de Estadística / Statistics Spain). [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-server-6E56CF)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) ![Transport](https://img.shields.io/badge/transport-stdio%20%7C%20Streamable%20HTTP-0A7EA4) [![License: EUPL 1.2](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-EUPL%201.2-blue.svg)](LICENSE.md) ![Read-only](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-read--only-lightgrey.svg) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Connect a client](#connect-a-client) · [Available tools](#available-tools) · [Available operations](#available-operations) **English** · [Spanish](README.es.md)
--- Give your AI assistant direct access to Statistics Spain's official statistics. This server lets any MCP client (Claude, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Zed and others) query the public JSON API of the **INE** (Instituto Nacional de Estadística, Statistics Spain). Ask in plain language, for example *"What was the unemployment rate for men in Murcia over the last four quarters?"*, and the assistant will find the right statistical operation, choose the table, resolve the filters and answer with the figures and a link to the official INE table. | | | | --- | --- | | **Hosted endpoint** | Available soon (meanwhile, [run it locally](#run-locally)) | | **Transport** | `stdio` (default) or Streamable HTTP | | **Authentication** | None, the data is public | | **Coverage** | Spain and its territorial breakdowns (autonomous communities, provinces, municipalities…) | | **Language** | Tool descriptions in English; data labels in Spanish, as INE publishes them | | **Catalogue** | 166 operations, 110 with tables available today ([full list](Resources/Catalogue.md)) | **Why use it** - **Real data, not memory.** Every figure is fetched from INE's API at request time. - **A guided path.** Five tools must be called in order; the server rejects skipped steps and identifiers it never returned. - **Always sourced.** Each result includes the operation, the table, its public URL and the filters applied. - **Quick.** Every step takes several requests at once and resolves them in parallel.

## Baserow: build databases, automations, apps & agents with AI — no code

Baserow is the secure, open-source platform for building databases, applications,
automations, and AI agents — all without code. Trusted by over 150,000 users, Baserow
delivers enterprise-grade security with GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2 Type II compliance, plus
cloud and self-hosted deployments for full data control. With a built-in AI Assistant
that lets you create databases and workflows using natural language, Baserow empowers
teams to structure data, automate processes, build internal tools, and create custom
dashboards. Fully extensible and API-first, Baserow integrates seamlessly with your
existing tools and performs at any scale.

* A spreadsheet database hybrid combining ease of use and powerful data organization.
* Create applications and portals, and publish them on your own domain.
* Automate repetitive workflows with automations.
* Visualize your data with dashboards.
* Kuma, powerful AI-assistant to builds complete solutions.
* GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2 Type II compliant.
* Easily self-hosted with no storage restrictions or sign-up on https://baserow.io to
  get started immediately.
* Best Alternative to Airtable.
* Open-core with all non-premium and non-enterprise features under
  the [MIT License](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/) allowing commercial and
  private use.
* Headless and API first.
* Uses popular frameworks and tools like [Django](https://www.djangoproject.com/),
  [Vue.js](https://vuejs.org/) and [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/).

[![Deploy to Heroku](https://www.herokucdn.com/deploy/button.svg)](https://www.heroku.com/deploy/?template=https://github.com/baserow/baserow/tree/master)

```bash
docker run -v baserow_data:/baserow/data -p 80:80 -p 443:443 baserow/baserow:2.4.3
```

# Quivr

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/The-Vibe-Company/quivr)

**An open-source engine for content that keeps arriving: store it, search it, and get
alerted when something new matches a topic you follow.**

You send Quivr documents (news articles, emails, posts, PDFs), or let it collect them
from RSS feeds, Microsoft 365 mailboxes and X lists. Quivr keeps every version, makes
each document searchable within seconds, and checks it against your saved alerts. Your
application talks to Quivr over an HTTP API; Quivr has no user interface of its own.

Quivr is developed by [The Vibe Company](https://www.thevibecompany.co), the AI agency
created by the Quivr team.

> **Status: Quivr 2.** From 2.0.0 on, the HTTP API (`/v0`) stays compatible across
> 2.x releases and upgrades keep your data in place; see
> [Versions and compatibility](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/reference/compatibility)
> and [Known limits](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/reference/known-limits).

## What you can do with it

- **Collect content** you send one by one or in batches, or that Quivr pulls from
  sources on a schedule. Files such as PDFs are read by plugins.
- **Search** by keywords, by meaning, or both. Every result points to the exact passage,
  document and version it comes from, so you can always cite it. Search up to 16
  corpora together. New corpora have their own partitions in the search index.
- **Follow a topic.** Save an alert such as `"harbour strike" AND (ferry OR port)`, or a
  plain-language description, and Quivr records every new document that matches, with
  the reason. Your application reads the matches or receives them as signed webhooks.
- **Keep history.** A correction becomes a new version; the old one stays readable. A
  withdrawn document leaves search at once, and alerts that caught it are told.
- **Plug in your own logic.** File formats, sources, embedding models, ranking and alert
  rules are plugins: small HTTP services you can replace, in any language.
- **Opt in to source and record visibility** for delegated reads with
  `visibility_mode: enforce`. [Configure delegated access](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/reference/configuration#delegated-reads).
- **Audit access and changes.** List or export sensitive actions and permission refusals
  by actor, and enable auditing for reads and searches through configuration.

candidates.readme_excerpt:
Your agents have a voice now.

Heard (heard.dev) is the voice context layer for agents on macOS: text-to-speech for Claude Code and Codex. When your agent finishes, fails or needs your approval, Heard tells you in a sentence or two, so you can step away and still know what's going on.
The engine in this repo is open source (Apache 2.0) and can speak locally with Kokoro text-to-speech, no account or API keys.

Comparing macOS coding-agent notification tools? A sound or a banner tells you something happened. Heard tells you what happened: a spoken summary of the work itself, across every session and every agent.
